11. Determination of Significance by Local Officials Having Jurisdiction of the Section 4(f) Land
A statement of the significance of the Section 4(f) Lands as determined by the agency official having jurisdiction of these lands (Cook County Forest Preserve District) would be antithesis to the Forest Preserve Law. The Illinois Revised Statutes, Chapter 57-1/2, Section 5, states the following:
"Any Forest Preserve District organized under this Act shall have the power to create forest preserves, and for that purpose shall have the power to acquire in fee simple in the manner hereinafter provided, and hold lands containing one or more natural forests or parts thereof, or land or lands connecting such forests or parts thereof, or lands capable of being re-forested, for the purpose of protecting and preserving the flora, fauna, and scenic beauties within such district, and to restore, restock, protect, and preserve the natural forests and said lands together with their flora and fauna, as nearly as may be in their natural state and condition for the purpose of the education, pleasure and recreation of the public....."
The recently published Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission's Open Space Report cites the need for 58,000 additional acres of open space in Cook County. Erosion of any holdings for non-open space use is significant however small the acreage may appear to be in relationship to the whole and would be contrary to the Cook County Forest Preserve District Land Policy.
The Cook County Forest Preserve District has stated in their Letter Dated September 4, 1974:
"It is our opinion that the temporary use will not have any significant effect on the recreational opportunities of the community".
The letter from the Cook County Forest Preserve along with other Coordination Correspondence are contained in Appendix A.
